subject: Unit-econ acceptance gates + evaluation timeline for MAP (POC scope)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Trent <emily.trent@calyxhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unit-econ acceptance gates + evaluation timeline for MAP (POC scope)

Emily —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To keep the MAP moving toward a June–July POC start, attached is a concise unit-econ worksheet and a suggested set of acceptance gates we usually run for pilot MAPs. Key asks for you to confirm:

- Average tokens per call we should model (prompt + expected completion).
- Target latency SLO (p95) for interactive flows — helps decide batching window.
- Whether you want prefix/KV caching on the patient ontology lookups (saves ~45–70% tokens on repeats).
- Targeted run-rate (QPS) during POC and expected concurrency.

I’ve pre-filled conservative defaults in RDW-UnitEcon-worksheet.xlsx (attached): 800 tokens/call, 0.8 RPCs per user action, 100 qps baseline. If anything looks off, flag it and we’ll iterate.

High-level acceptance gates we propose for the MAP (short):
1) Unit cost <= $0.003/token effective (after caching/batching) for the primary generate route
2) End-to-end p95 latency <= 500ms for fast UI flows (can relax to 700ms for bulk scoring)
3) Quality: BLEU/ROUGE proxies on our eval set show no >6% regression vs baseline model
4) Operational: model fallback and circuit-breaker verified in canary

I’ll share a version of the MAP milestone PDF with dates if you’re good with the above.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: RDW-UnitEcon-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12kb), MAP-Milestones-2026.pdf (overview, 45kb)

From: Emily Trent <emily.trent@calyxhealth.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@calyxhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unit-econ acceptance gates + evaluation timeline for MAP (POC scope)

Hi Soojin —

Thanks — this format is exactly what our procurement and engineering teams need. A couple quick clarifications:

- Tokens: Current backend telemetry suggests ~1,200 tokens per user session (we talked about shorter prompts earlier — 800 may be optimistic unless we cache aggressively).
- Latency: We need interactive flows at p95 <= 450ms for triage UI; 500–700ms acceptable for batch scoring jobs.
- Caching: Yes, we'll enable prefix caching for the ontology lookups. We expect around 55% repetition on the calls in week 1 of the POC.
- Run-rate: Start with 25 qps for initial POC (pilot group ~50 users), plan to scale to 150 qps during expansion.

Procurement looped in for the timeline and any contract/redline items. Can you add a short worked example (tokens/$ calculation) in the worksheet showing the caching benefit and batching impact per 1k requests? That will make the CFO comfortable.

Emily
Emily Trent
Product Lead — Integrations, CalyxHealth
emily.trent@calyxhealth.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Trent <emily.trent@calyxhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@calyxhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unit-econ acceptance gates + evaluation timeline for MAP (POC scope)

Emily —

Great notes. I updated RDW-UnitEcon-worksheet.xlsx with two worked examples (tab names: "CacheOn + 25qps", "NoCache + 150qps") and added a simple batching sensitivity table (batch sizes 1/4/8/16) showing marginal token savings vs latency. Summary of the calculations we added:

- Baseline model cost (Redwood hosted price used for planning): $0.0008 per 1k tokens (example pricing for quantized LLM variant in doc) — conservative placeholder; final billing subject to contract profile.
- Effective tokens per request (example rows):
  - No caching: 1,200 tokens => cost/request = $0.00096
  - With prefix caching (55% hit): avg tokens = 540 => cost/request = $0.000432
  - With batching (batch size 8, amortize prompt overhead): effective tokens/request down ~12–18% depending on sequence length

Worked number: at 25 qps, 1,200 tokens/no-cache => ~$2,080/day; with 55% cache hit and batch size 4 => ~$940/day (rough).

Acceptance gates updated slightly to reflect your latency ask: p95 interactive <= 450ms. I also added a gating checklist we use for procurement: SLA targets, data residency note, and a simple rollback plan.

Link to the updated folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdE-example (view-only for your team).

Next suggested milestones (high level):
- Week 0 (sign): Contract + data access + initial model pinning
- Week 1–2 (setup): Environment + telemetry + small test corpus (50–100 users)
- Week 3 (eval): Run curated eval set, run 1k simulated requests for latency/cost sensitivity
- Week 4 (canary): 10% traffic canary with fallback to smaller model variant
- Week 6 (POC close): Final acceptance and go/no-go decision

Ben and Marcus — flag anything missing on cost calc or rollout sequencing.

Thanks,
Soojin

Subject: Re: Unit-econ acceptance gates + evaluation timeline for MAP (POC scope)

Looping in quick cost math I ran from the worksheet so we have a clean ask for the CFO:

Assumptions used:
- Redwood hosted unit price used for planning: $0.0008 per 1k tokens
- Avg tokens/session (no-cache): 1,200; with 55% cache hit => effective 540 tokens
- Batching: realistic batch size 4 during interactive peaks (latency trade-off kept within 450ms)

Annualized simplified view (scale scenario):
- 25 qps steady-state pilot => ~2.16M requests/day => This is just for example, we highlighted daily numbers in the sheet.
- Pilot monthly cost (25 qps, 30 days):
  - No cache: ~ $62k/month
  - With cache + batching (as described): ~ $28k/month

Recommendation: include dedicated reserved capacity quote in the MAP if Calyx expects steady expansion to >100 qps — dedicated reduces unit by ~35–45% in our models and fixes latency SLOs.

I added a short appendix in the worksheet tab "dedicated-vs-hosted" with break-even at ~400k requests/day.

Marcus
